title: Stop the catalogue from holding a copy of every currency code

blocks.text: The Nordic shop loads its supplier's price list, four million products, into memory every night. A heap dump shows four million `"SEK"` strings and four million `"SE"` strings, one of each per product, each its own object. Every SKU and every product name is different; currencies and countries come from a handful of values.

The loader already has a table, `codes`, which it drops with the catalogue when the next price list replaces it, and `tableSize()` reports its size to the shop's metrics. Finish the `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/CatalogueLoader.java`:

items: `shared(value)`: the one string the loader keeps for `value`'s text;

cases.says: each line of the price list becomes a product with its SKU, name, currency and country
two products with the same currency and country hold the same String objects for them
the loader's table holds the few currencies and countries, not every SKU and name

origin.section: Equal Strings Built at Run Time Are Separate Objects; intern() Shares One Only with Code That Keeps Its Result

concepts: intern() returns the pooled string with the same characters and can't change the string it is called on, so only code that stores the returned reference shares one copy.
Sharing equal strings pays only for fields with few distinct values; interning unique values adds a table entry each and saves nothing.
